speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me when the wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions first started?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota, have you noticed any expanding red rings or tick bites on your skin? I also need to know if the skin lesions are painful or itchy, and whether you have experienced any joint swelling in other areas besides the wrist.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those painless violaceous lesions on your hands and wrists, combined with the joint pain and recent camping trip, are highly suggestive of Lyme disease. I need to confirm this with specific blood work, so REQUEST TEST: Lyme_Serology.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Lyme serology results make Lyme disease unlikely, so I need to consider other causes like disseminated gonococcal infection or meningococcemia. Can you tell me if you have had any recent sexual contact without protection, and do you have a headache or neck stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to confirm the source of this infection, so REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture. I also need to see the appearance of the lesions, so REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The combination of tenosynovitis, dermatitis with painless vesiculopustular lesions, and fever in a sexually active young adult is classic for Disseminated Gonococcal Infection. I will proceed with a definitive diagnosis based on this clinical triad.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
